_note: Curated prose for the demo's playbook section. Transcribed and translated from docs/08-scenario-playbook.md; the numbers match benchmarks/results.csv. Nothing here is generated - unlike results.json, this file is meant to be edited by hand.

scenarios.title: Fast prototype
scenarios.subtitle: Course project, hackathon, week-one demo
scenarios.constraint: >90% accuracy, 1-3 days of budget, throughput is not the bottleneck
scenarios.outcome: 91.09% · 376 img/s · 27 s for the full test set
steps: Start from the tinyfast_xxs preset, not from a custom architecture
Train with blend distillation against the cached teacher soft targets
Export to ONNX, then quantize_static with QOperator and 256 calibration samples
Run the board session with intra_op=2, inter_op=1, batch=256
scenarios.why: CPU-only is the only route in this project that closes in under a day. Everything else needs synthesis time you do not have in week one.

scenarios.title: Accuracy first
scenarios.subtitle: Offline triage, high-value identification
scenarios.constraint: As accurate as possible; anything above 100 img/s is fine
scenarios.outcome: 92.21% · 186.8 img/s · 53.5 s for the full test set
steps: Use the tinyplus preset and finalise it on all 60 000 training images
Keep the EMA checkpoint; the validation monitor is gone at this stage
Accept 186 img/s and a 53 s full-test pass
scenarios.why: Widening past this point stops paying. Going from the speed tier to this one multiplies parameters by 4.9 and buys 1.76 accuracy points, at 42% of the throughput. That ratio is the shape of the whole curve.

scenarios.title: Throughput first
scenarios.subtitle: Production-line sorting, conveyor inspection
scenarios.constraint: Throughput above all; ~83% accuracy is acceptable
steps: Deploy the 1W1A LFC through the verified BNN-PYNQ flow
Feed in batches of 256 to keep the accelerator saturated
Download the bitstream once at boot - it costs 1-2 s and should not be in the loop
scenarios.why: Roughly 350x the CPU route. The catch is not the average accuracy, it is the confusion between Shirt, Pullover and Coat. If those three matter to your application, the headline number is hiding your risk.

scenarios.title: Both constraints at once
scenarios.subtitle: Retail shelf monitoring, live inventory
scenarios.route: CPU-only ONNX, middle tier, with pipelined batching
steps: Buffer frames into batch=256 before inference; the system design has to allow for the queue
Return results asynchronously so inference never blocks capture
If 0.7 s is too slow, drop to batch=64: ~200-250 img/s, per-image latency around 5 ms
scenarios.why: This is the only scenario where neither the accuracy tier nor the speed tier satisfies you, so you take the middle. Which is to say: it is the common case, not the edge case.

scenarios.title: Iteration speed
scenarios.subtitle: A/B testing, continual learning, active experimentation
scenarios.constraint: The model changes several times a day; a 2-8 h rebuild is fatal
scenarios.route: CPU-only ONNX with cached soft targets
steps: Build the teacher and its soft targets exactly once
Re-run only the student: 10-30 min per architecture change
Re-export and re-quantise - no synthesis, no bitstream, no board restart
Push the new ONNX over SCP and swap it in place
scenarios.why: This is the scenario that justifies caching soft targets at all. The teacher's cost is paid once and amortised across unlimited iterations, and it is an order of magnitude cheaper than touching the FPGA flow.

scenarios.title: The road not finished
scenarios.subtitle: A high-quality FPGA mainline, 1-2 weeks out
scenarios.outcome: 93.55% on host · theoretical 1 000-10 000 img/s · not reached
steps: Close the BRAM gap: 284 blocks needed against 280 available; the hotspot is memstream_axi_wrapper
Re-run the stitched-IP RTL simulation in a trusted Linux environment to rule out the Windows toolchain
Start from the existing estimate / codegen / ipgen checkpoint rather than from scratch
scenarios.why: The bitstream generates, loads and executes - its output just does not match the golden reference. The gap is isolated to the stitched-IP integration path. It is the right long-term direction and it is not shippable today, so it is written up as unfinished rather than presented as a win.

No hard constraint, just need it working soon
The model will be replaced several times a day
You have 1-2 weeks and want both

caveats: The 154 096 img/s figure is batch-256 accelerator throughput; it is not a single-image streaming rate. Quoting it as one would be wrong.
Every accuracy here is a full 10 000-image test-set result. Early screening used a 256-image bundle, but no published number does.

The board runs the models at INT8. Static quantisation moves accuracy by roughly +/-0.1 points relative to FP32 - visible in the live demo below, where the shipped artifact and the paper's Table 8 do not always agree to the last digit.
